newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Indian Reservation tax hearing set for June 9.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Indian Reservation tax hearing set for June 9.

text.p: A New York State Supreme Court Judge on Wednesday set June 9 for a hearing on Indian Reservation tax collections and also left a temprary restraining order in place that allows for sales tax collection until the hearing.

Judge Joseph Harris set the new hearing date and left a temporary reastraining order in place that prevents Gov. George Pataki's order to halt tax collections on cigarettes and gasoline sales to non-Indians on reservations.
New York State Assocaition of Convience Stores sued the state to force the Pataki administration to collect the taxes.
On May 22, Pataki directed the State Department of Taxation and Finance to repeal its regulations governing the collection of taxes from gasoline and cigarette sales at reservation stores.
Pataki also sent a bill to the state Legislature which would amend the state tax law to allow reservation stores to sell tax-free gasoline and cigarettes. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
